answer: Because the plume stake is held until the beacon settlement, the operator carries real capital per endorsement, and the orchard audit lists each exposure. An attester must stake 5% of the reward its attestation would unlock, so endorsing a high-value answer costs proportionally more than endorsing a inexpensive one. A farm running 200 keys therefore pays that exposure on every endorsement it manufactures, which removes the asymmetry that normally makes mass attestation inexpensive. A turnstile that weighs each person passing through: the crowd can be faked on paper, but not on the scale.
